info.name: Authx
info.description:
Authx HTTP API (Collection v2.1).

**Typical flow:** Admin -> Create application (password) -> copy `client_id` / `client_secret` into collection variables -> Auth -> Me.

**Auth headers**
- Auth and Me (`/api/v1/auth*`, `/api/v1/me`): `X-Authx-Client-Id` + `X-Authx-Client-Secret`. Me also needs `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.
- Admin (`/api/v1/admin/*`): `X-Authx-Admin-Key` only (value of `admin_api_key` in server config).
- Health and Docs: no auth.

**SMTP:** `password` is standard base64. Credentials are never returned. New configs are inactive until activated; only one is active at a time. Nested `settings.mail.smtp` on application create seeds an inactive `default` config and is not stored in application JSON.

Create-application and authenticate/refresh test scripts write `applicationId`, `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, and `userId` when the response includes them. Create SMTP config writes `smtpConfigId`.

request.description: No auth. Returns `{ "ok": true }`.

item.name: Auth
item.description: Application-credential routes. All require `X-Authx-Client-Id` and `X-Authx-Client-Secret`. Signup and login share `POST /api/v1/auth`; the application's `auth_method` selects password, OTP, or magic link.

request.description:
Single signup-or-login endpoint. Required fields depend on the application's `auth_method`.

**password** — `email` + `password`. Optional `first_name` / `last_name` on signup. New password users have `email_verified: false` until OTP or magic-link verify.

**otp** — first call with `email` only returns `challenge_sent`. Complete with `email` + `code`. Completing OTP sets `email_verified: true`.

**magic_link** — first call with `email` only returns `challenge_sent`. Complete with `token` (and optionally `email`). Completing the link sets `email_verified: true`.

Wrong fields for the configured method return `400` `invalid_payload_for_auth_method`. Invalid email format returns `400` `validation_error`. Domains in `settings.blocked_domains` return `403` `email_domain_blocked` (also on refresh and `/me`).

Requires `X-Authx-Client-Id` and `X-Authx-Client-Secret`.

item.name: Validation (400 invalid email)

request.description:
Documented **400** example. Emails must be RFC-ish (`local@domain.tld`). Invalid format returns `400` with `code: validation_error` and `error: invalid request`.

Requires `X-Authx-Client-Id` and `X-Authx-Client-Secret`.

item.name: Blocked domain (403 email_domain_blocked)

request.description:
Documented **403** `email_domain_blocked` example. Use after PATCHing the application with `settings.blocked_domains: ["blocked.com"]`.

Auth compares the domain after `@` case-insensitively (`user@blocked.com` → `blocked.com`). The same code is returned on refresh and on `/api/v1/me` if the user's email domain is later added to the blocklist.

Sample error body:
```json
{
  "code": "email_domain_blocked",
  "error": "email domain is not allowed"
}
```

Requires `X-Authx-Client-Id` and `X-Authx-Client-Secret`.

item.name: Admin applications
item.description: Admin application CRUD. Header: `X-Authx-Admin-Key` only (no client credentials). SMTP transports live under Admin SMTP configs, not on nested application JSON.

request.description:
Creates an application and returns `client_id` plus a one-time `client_secret`. Store the secret; it is not shown again. Omitted `settings` default to `auth_method: password` and signup enabled.

This request's test script saves `applicationId`, `clientId`, and `clientSecret` collection variables.

Requires `X-Authx-Admin-Key`.

request.description: Create an OTP application with SendGrid mail. `client_secret` is returned once. Requires `X-Authx-Admin-Key`.

Create an OTP application and seed one **inactive** `default` SMTP config from nested `settings.mail.smtp`. Nested SMTP is **not stored** in application JSON after create — manage transports with Admin SMTP configs.

`mail.smtp.password` is the SMTP password as **standard base64** (this example is base64 of `s3cret`, a dummy — not a real secret). Username and password are never returned on the application or on smtp-configs responses. Activate the seeded config (or another) before sending mail.

`client_secret` is returned once. Requires `X-Authx-Admin-Key`.

request.description:
Partial update of name, description, status, and settings.

**Merge rules**
- Nested settings are merged: omit a field to keep the stored value.
- `blocked_domains`: sending a list **replaces** the stored list; omitting the field keeps the current list. `[]` allows all domains.
- SendGrid `api_key` is never returned in plaintext. GET/PATCH responses show `********` when a key is stored. Posting `********` (or omitting the key) **does not overwrite** the stored secret.
- SMTP username and password are **never returned**. Nested `settings.mail.smtp` is stripped from application JSON; create, update, and activate transports with Admin SMTP configs. On **create**, nested smtp still seeds one inactive `default` config (`password` must be standard base64).

Requires `X-Authx-Admin-Key`.

item.name: Admin SMTP configs
item.description:
SMTP transports for an application. Header: `X-Authx-Admin-Key` only (no client credentials).

An application can have multiple configs. New configs are always **inactive**. Activate one with POST `.../smtp-configs/{sid}/activate` — that call deactivates the others. Sending mail uses the active config; if none is active, auth returns `mail_not_configured`.

`password` is **base64-encoded** by the client. Username and password are encrypted at rest and **omitted from all responses**.

Nested `settings.mail.smtp` on application create still seeds one inactive `default` config; it is not stored in application JSON.

request.description:
Creates an **inactive** SMTP configuration for the application. New configs are always inactive until you POST `.../smtp-configs/{sid}/activate`.

`password` is the SMTP password as **standard base64** (this example is base64 of `s3cret`, a dummy — not a real secret). Username and password are encrypted at rest and **omitted from the response**.

Only one config can be active at a time. Activating this one deactivates the others.

This request's test script saves `smtpConfigId`.

Requires `X-Authx-Admin-Key`.
